analysis:
Both changed files are offline CI regression tests (scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py, scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py). No provider runtime, coordinator, attestation, key custody or prefix-cache code is touched, so T-041 and the TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-011 boundaries are unaffected by these edits.

The changes add a mimo_audio routing component and tests that gate the 1.87 GB codec fetch on it. They also add tests for the CI workflow wiring that these files assert: (a) cache saves limited to push events on master/dev, with PR runs unable to save; (b) a .git cache restore and fsck validation that falls back to a cold checkout; (c) checkouts with persist-credentials: false, so tokens are not cached in .git/config; (d) sparse checkout excluding docs/reports/evidence and landing/public/media; (e) a SwiftPM repository cache keyed on runner layout and lane.

These assertions tighten CI hygiene: the cache-poisoning surface from PR runs is reduced, and no secrets, environment, id-token or repository checkouts are permitted (test lines ~252-267 in head). The truth-table test for the provider gate still ensures a failed or cancelled lane cannot pass.

The actual workflow YAML, the composite action, ci-component-paths.py and docs-impact.yml are not in the supplied evidence, so I can't confirm the real wiring matches these assertions. A restored .git cache from master pushes is only integrity-checked by fsck --connectivity-only, which is a pre-existing design choice and not a regression visible here. No concrete security regression found. Integration should confirm the production workflow matches the asserted save and credential policy.
